#### FAQS

## Questions teams ask before they start

What's the actual difference between agentic AI and a chatbot layered on our data?

A chatbot answers questions against whatever data it's pointed at, with no guarantee the answer is correct or explainable. An agent reasons over a governed data model and only reads from certified sources. For example, Syren's [OTIF-D solution](https://syrencloud.com/on-time-in-full/) for a global HLS supply chain, the Conversational OTIF Agent answers questions like "which SKUs missed OTIF in Region X last week, and why?" directly against certified data, not a live guess against raw tables.

How does Syren make sure an agent's outputs are accurate and not hallucinated?

Testing & Validation is a dedicated stage, and includes validating model accuracy against real-world business scenarios, formal bias and fairness testing, performance/stress testing for model drift, and a human-in-the-loop evaluation step before go-live. Post-deployment, MLOps Automation adds continuous observability, monitoring performance, drift, and anomalies, so accuracy is tracked on an ongoing basis.

How should CIOs and CDOs think about rolling this out across the organization, not just as a single agent?

The useful model is a maturity ladder, not a leap: Data Engineering → BI → Machine Learning → Predictive Analytics → Optimization → Generative AI → Agentic AI → Autonomous Enterprise. Agentic AI depends on the governance and data foundation built in the earlier rungs, which is why engagements must start with a Governance & Compliance Framework and Use Case Identification before any agent is built.

The practical sequencing CIOs and CDOs must get right: govern and unify the data first, prove ROI on one well-scoped use case (Syren's own delivery has run 200+ certified professionals and 20+ engagements to a 94% client satisfaction rate across industries from retail to manufacturing to life sciences), then scale persona by persona, rather than announcing an enterprise AI initiative and building the governance model retroactively once something goes wrong.

Is this proven in production, or mostly pilots and proofs of concept?

Syren has deployed 20+ commercial agentic AI solutions, backed by 100+ commercial SMEs across domains and 200+ certified professionals in commercial data science, data engineering, and GenAI, across 20+ Commercial Excellence engagements. These are production accelerators with quantified results (e.g., 8–10% revenue increase from Sales Captain.AI), not conceptual pilots.

Should we build one flagship agent first, or roll agents out across every function at once?

One well-scoped use case first, proven and measured, then expand — this is the pattern that avoids the common failure mode of a flashy pilot with no path to enterprise-wide trust. Syren’s Agent Operationalization Framework (Discovery → Configuration → Operationalize → Monitor → Evaluate) is designed for exactly this: the Evaluate stage forces a real ROI check against the original business case before anyone talks about scaling it to the next function or Lead agent.

What's the difference between your GenAI Model Engineering and just using an off-the-shelf LLM API?

An off-the-shelf API gives you a general-purpose model with no domain knowledge of your business. Syren's GenAI Model Engineering layer adds model fine-tuning and domain alignment (injecting your proprietary terminology and KPIs), inference speed and cost optimization, continuous learning through active feedback loops, and ongoing performance monitoring and retraining. The result is a model that stays accurate and cost-efficient as your business changes.

Can Syren's agents integrate with our existing ERP, CRM, and BI tools, or do we need new systems?

Integration with your existing stack is a named part of the Agentic AI & ML Integration offering, specifically Enterprise System Connectivity into ERP, CRM, BI, and cloud platforms, combined with Intelligent Workflow Orchestration for real-time decisions. Most engagements are built to connect into what you already run rather than requiring a system replacement.
